page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 945 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data shows average performance across most compute and memory metrics, with specific top-tier capabilities in compression and lightweight inference. The single-threaded gzip compression reaches 36.52 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 15.37 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% tier. For LLM inference, text generation using a small 135M model performs at a top-tier rate of 343.48 tokens/sec. Other benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark database operations, fall within the average range.

Given its high memory density of 8 GB per vCPU and integrated 945 GB NVMe SSD, the E16ds_v7 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX also supports specialized vector and matrix operations.
